tally.headline: 8 of 12 gradeable claims held up, 2 did not

implied_side.why: EdgeDesk’s own number sat 2.6 points toward New York Giants of the quote EdgeDesk captured at DraftKings. That is what the disagreement implied. It was published as research, not as a recommendation to bet it.

implied_total.why: EdgeDesk’s fair total of 49.3 sat 1.8 points above the captured total of 47.5.

closing_line.why: no closing line is held for this game: the Collective captured none and the schedule feed carries none. Closing-line value is left blank rather than estimated from the result.

reasons: 7 claims held up, 1 held up in direction only and 2 did not. Parts of the read were right and parts were not.
EdgeDesk projected a home margin of 6.9 and the game finished 22 the home way — 15.1 points of margin error, inside the range the model published.
process.basis: the drivers, matchups and measured advantages only — never the price or the market claim, which are the result in longer words

variance_markers.label: A 22-point margin
variance_markers.text: Once a game is this far apart both teams stop playing the game they were rated on — the leader runs clock, the trailer throws — so late-game rates describe the situation rather than either team.

verdict.line: The number did not land and the reasoning half held. There is something here to investigate without concluding the model is broken.

grading.separation_note: The bet result and the process grade above are computed separately and are allowed to disagree. A winning number with a broken thesis is recorded as exactly that.

lessons.pregame_expectation: 2 published claims said the same thing: New York Giants holds the largest measured edge in this matchup: New York Giants +0.044 (#6 of 32) vs Los Angeles Rams +0.028 (#13 of 32) — 7 places on the league board. New York Giants’ run offence rates +0.044 (#6 of 32) and Los Angeles Rams’ run defence rates +0.001 (#16 of 32). Added the way the model adds them, this pairing sits +0.045 from the league mean, which favours New York Giants.
lessons.actual_result: New York Giants 2.48 yards per carry against Los Angeles Rams 5.82; New York Giants 52 rushing yards against Los Angeles Rams 163. New York Giants 2.48 yards per carry against Los Angeles Rams 5.82; New York Giants 52 rushing yards against Los Angeles Rams 163.
lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk named New York Giants as better in rushing and the game went the other way, across 2 separate published claims. One game does not overturn a season-long rating, but this is the direction to watch: every signal this claim rests on went the other way
lessons.suggested_investigation: These claims carried 2.2 points of the published number between them and were contradicted. Check whether the same category has been contradicted in other games this season before touching anything.

lessons.pregame_expectation: 1 of the claims in this article rested on model.
lessons.actual_result: None of them could be graded: no single-game statistic in EdgeDesk’s vocabulary observes this driver.
lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk prices these games partly on signals it has no way to observe afterwards. That is not an error in the model — it is a gap in the audit, and it means the platform cannot tell, from results alone, whether those parts of the number are earning their weight.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Consider whether a postgame data source exists for model.

lessons.pregame_expectation: EdgeDesk published a fair total of 49.3.
lessons.actual_result: The game finished with 34 points, an error of 15.3.
lessons.lesson: A total missed by this much usually means a pace or a finishing assumption was wrong, not that both ratings were. Check which of the two moved.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Was the play count or the points per drive the miss? Both are in this game’s result record.

lessons.pregame_expectation: EdgeDesk makes it Los Angeles Rams -6.9 where the market has Los Angeles Rams -9.5 at DraftKings — a 2.6 points disagreement.
lessons.actual_result: Los Angeles Rams won by 22. the result landed on EdgeDesk’s side of the market number: Los Angeles Rams beat a margin of 9.5
lessons.lesson: The disagreement landed. One landing proves nothing on its own; the aggregate of them, held against the closing line, is the only thing that would.
